title: Toes in the Mud
note: b384 — first use of 'hoe', 'furrow', 'deer', and footprint's earth-toned o.key variant.

pages.brief: Close on Ned's orange webbed feet completely caked in thick brown mud, seen from above. He is looking down at them, unimpressed.
pages.alt: A close view of Ned's webbed feet completely caked in thick brown mud, seen from above, as he looks down at them unimpressed.

pages.brief: Ned hopping on one foot clutching the other, beak open, having stubbed his toe on a half-buried stone. Very funny.
pages.alt: Ned hops on one foot clutching the other, beak open, having stubbed his toe on a half-buried stone. Very funny.

pages.brief: Interior of the garden shed: Pip holding up an old wooden-handled hoe far bigger than himself, presenting the solution.
pages.note: indoors still gets a real ground + sky backdrop, not 'plain' (b384 batch-2 review fix).
pages.alt: Inside the garden shed, Pip holds up an old wooden-handled hoe far bigger than himself, presenting the solution.

pages.brief: Ned dragging the hoe through the mud with both wings, leaning right back into it, cutting a deep furrow. Real effort.
pages.alt: Ned drags the hoe through the mud with both wings, leaning right back into the effort, cutting a deep furrow.

pages.brief: A deer bounding across the far end of the garden, legs stretched, seen in silhouette through the gap in the hedge. Elegant and sudden.
pages.alt: A deer bounds across the far end of the garden, legs stretched, seen through the gap in the hedge — elegant and sudden.

pages.brief: The deer at full speed in the middle distance, all four feet off the ground, drawn with real grace. Both friends watching, stopped mid-action.
pages.alt: The deer runs at full speed in the middle distance, all four feet off the ground, while both friends watch, stopped mid-action.

pages.brief: Close on the deer's slender feet touching the ground and leaving almost no mark, contrasted with Ned's great muddy prints beside them.
pages.alt: A close view of the deer's slender feet touching the ground and leaving almost no mark, contrasted with Ned's great muddy prints beside them.

pages.brief: Closing page: Ned and Pip sitting on the hoe handle in the evening sun, feet clean now, the dug bed neat behind them. Satisfied.
pages.alt: Closing page: Ned and Pip sit together in the evening sun, feet clean now, the dug bed neat behind them. Satisfied.
